transcript:
Header: 2026-09-23 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jia Huang (Redwood SRE), Aisha Malik (Novapay CTO), Tom Reed (Novapay ML Eng), Marcus Lee (Novapay Infra)

Summary: quick recap of last week's benchmark, looked at throughput cliff at ~520 rps, tail latency increases after 10s queueing window. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Lena Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um let's do a quick check-in. Samir you ran the new throughput run yesterday right?
[00:12] Samir Patel: Yep, ran three sweeps. We did baseline (no batch), continuous batching enabled, and continuous batching + KV cache priming. Results were... kinda expected but there are some surprises at higher conc.
[00:26] Aisha Malik: Quick note, we're still targeting ~600 reqs per second for peak with 95ms p95 target on the payments UI flows, just so context.
[00:38] Tom Reed: yeah we want to avoid any tail spikes that cause retries, that kills UX.
[00:44] Samir Patel: Right, so with continuous batching on a single GPU node we saw stable throughput up to ~480 rps with p95 around 120ms, p99 ~420ms. When we pushed concurrency to 12 we hit a cliffing effect at ~520 rps where queue length started to balloon and p99 jumped to >1s.
[01:05] Marcus Lee: That cliff is worrying, is that due to KV cache misses or kernel swapping?
[01:12] Jia Huang: From the logs it looks like KV cash warming is a factor — we saw cold-starts for certain prompt prefixes; also the batching window got larger under higher conc which increased end-to-end latency for smaller requests.
[01:24] Samir Patel: Exactly; continuous batcher will group requests to improve throughput but if the window grows to collect more tokens it can hurt SLOs for low-latency requests. We need a balance: target concurrency and a max batch window.
[01:39] Lena Morales: Remind me of the config you used for the sweep?
[01:43] Samir Patel: Default continuous batching, max window 50ms, batch size uncapped, concurrency tests at 4,8,12,16. Also tried explicit queueing with a 2s max queue window in one run.
[01:55] Tom Reed: Which run hit the 1s p99? The 2s queue window or the uncapped?
[01:59] Samir Patel: The uncapped. The 2s queue window actually gave us a slightly better average throughput but tail got worse because requests waited longer until batch was full.
[02:12] Aisha Malik: So we need a policy that prioritizes low-latency payment requests — can we do priority queues?
[02:18] Jia Huang: We can. Redwood supports route-level priority and small-batch fast-paths. We can reserve a fraction of capacity for low-latency traffic and let bulk operations go on a slower path.
[02:28] Marcus Lee: That sounds good — but does that change our cost? If we reserve capacity we might need extra nodes.
[02:33] Lena Morales: There are a couple levers: reserved capacity (Dedicated) or route-level throttles on Hosted. We can also tune concurrency per-route so payments route gets conc=4 and the background route conc=16.
[02:45] Tom Reed: Can we get numbers on cost delta for reserving 1 GPU for low-latency vs autoscaling fallback?
[02:51] Lena Morales: I'll include a delta in the pricing note. For the POC we can simulate reserved lanes without committing to Dedicated — it's a config-level reservation in the runtime.
[03:03] Samir Patel: Back to bench: with KV cache priming we saw p99 drop by ~30% in the worst case; mostly helps when prefix tokens are repeated. But for diverse prompts the benefit is smaller.
[03:18] Aisha Malik: Our real traffic is pretty mixed — a lot of templated payment messages but also ad-hoc natural language from support bots.
[03:26] Samir Patel: So a hybrid strategy might win: prime the KV cache for top N prefixes and use a small reserved fast-path for payment-critical endpoints. That keeps overall cost down but protects the SLOs.
[03:39] Jia Huang: Also if you can share a 24h sample trace we'll use that to build a simulated load that matches your mix — that will let us tune batching window and concurrency for realistic distributions.
[03:50] Aisha Malik: We can provide that, Tom will send a sample by EOD Thursday.
[03:55] Tom Reed: yep I'll anonymize and share.
[03:58] Samir Patel: Great. One other observation: when we pushed concurrency to 16 the scheduler started moving kernels to different paths and we saw memory pressure spikes and small GC pauses — that also inflated tail latency. Could be model execution kernel selection under high mem footprint.
[04:15] Marcus Lee: Is that something on Redwood side or model compiled artifact? We saw similar on our infra with older drivers.
[04:21] Jia Huang: Could be both — kernel selection heuristics depend on sequence length distribution; if there are long sequences it's more memory intensive. We recommend using quantized variants or lower memory kernels for those heavy tails.
[04:33] Samir Patel: We can try a stitched fallback: if queue > X then route to a 4-bit quantized model variant with similar quality. That drops latency but slightly affects output fidelity.
[04:44] Aisha Malik: How much quality drop? For transactions we need deterministic amounts and numbers to be accurate.
[04:50] Samir Patel: For simple instruction-following prompts quality delta is small; for multi-step generation there can be small hallucinations. We'd only use fallback for non-critical free-form routes.
[04:59] Lena Morales: Noted. We'll avoid fallbacks for the payments route.
[05:03] [05:03] break in audio / overlap
[05:07] Tom Reed: Regarding measurement, what metrics should we capture in the POC to show success?
[05:11] Jia Huang: p50/p95/p99 latency, queue length distribution, batch sizes distribution, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens. Also per-route throughput.
[05:22] Samir Patel: We'll dump the perf-run logs to a shared spreadsheet and include visualizations of queue length vs p99. I'll add a column for batch window times.
[05:30] Aisha Malik: Do you have an easy way to reproduce the exact driver stack? We run on slightly older nvidia drivers and that might be the cause for kernel variance.
[05:39] Samir Patel: We captured the environment: cuda 12.1 vs 12.2 differences can matter. I'll include driver and kernel info in the logs.
[05:47] Marcus Lee: Good. Also curious about autoscaling: can Redwood autoscale on queue length rather than CPU?
[05:53] Jia Huang: Yes, queue-backed autoscaling is supported; you can set a target queue length per shard and scale out when exceeded. That prevents long wait times building up.
[06:03] Tom Reed: Does that incur cold-start latencies when scaling?
[06:07] Samir Patel: There's some spin-up time for new pods/nodes — maybe 15-45s depending on infra — but we can use burst capacity pre-warmed nodes for quick scale. Dedicated offers faster spin-up.
[06:18] Aisha Malik: Ok — so action plan is clear. A few nitty-gritty questions: what concurrency per GPU do you recommend for our model size?
[06:27] Samir Patel: For the model you shared (7B dense-ish) we recommend conc 8-12 for throughput-heavy routes, and conc 2-4 for low-latency routes. But dependent on avg seq len; shorter sequences can tolerate higher concurrency.
[06:40] Tom Reed: Our avg token length is 60 but tail goes to 450 sometimes. That could explain memory pressure.
[06:46] Jia Huang: Exactly — you may want to cap per-request tokens or split large jobs to a background pipeline.
[06:52] Lena Morales: Quick recap before we move to scheduling next touch: Samir will run constrained-concurrency tests (4,8,12,16) with: (a) max batch window 25ms, (b) 50ms, (c) 2s queue window, and (d) KV priming on top. Upload logs and dashboard links. Jia to try KV priming config and share. Novapay to share 24h traces. Lena to send pricing and pilot extension.
[07:19] Aisha Malik: Sounds good. If we can see a run that hits 600 rps while keeping p95 under 200ms we can move forward to a short production pilot.
[07:28] Samir Patel: We'll try to get that target; initial runs indicate it's achievable with reserved fast-paths and primed cache.
[07:35] Lena Morales: Great — let's reconvene next Wednesday same time. I'll send calendar invite.
[07:40] Tom Reed: thanks all.
[07:42] Marcus Lee: Thanks.
[07:43] [End of recording]

References mentioned: shared spreadsheet link (internal), POC run dashboard (link), driver/kernel notes (will be attached).
